evidence.title: MultiCC: repo
evidence.locator: top-level archived, stargazers_count and default_branch fields
evidence.finding: The inspected lsjwzh/MultiCC repository metadata has archived=false and 15 stars. archived=false does not establish an active lifecycle.

evidence.title: MultiCC: releases
evidence.locator: row tag_name=v2.25.0: published_at, prerelease, html_url, body and assets
evidence.finding: Latest returned release by published_at is v2.25.0, published 2026-11-27T10:44:23Z, prerelease=false. Latest stable returned is v2.25.0 at 2026-11-27T10:44:23Z.

evidence.title: MultiCC: README.md
evidence.locator: Download MultiCC; Choose how to work; Quick Start; FAQ
evidence.finding: Documents public desktop installers, Android APK and iOS App Store link, standalone setup, local browser UI and self-hosted workspaces. The host/service must stay running.

evidence.title: MultiCC: docs/features.md
evidence.locator: Multi-provider support, Session orchestration, Task board, Long-running & scheduled work, dashboard and Git worktree management
evidence.finding: The feature reference gives exact terminal/chat launch modes, per-task state/worktrees, Commander dispatch, cron and event triggers, syntax-gated merges and Git actions.

evidence.title: MultiCC: docs/cli-switching.md
evidence.locator: Supported CLIs table and Chat sessions only; switching and native session reuse
evidence.finding: Documents Claude Code via Agent SDK in chat and CLI in terminal, Codex exec/app-server, and OpenCode run integration. Each engine retains its own native session, with a bounded visible handoff checkpoint.

evidence.title: MultiCC: src/cli-adapters/index.js
evidence.locator: createCliAdapters, imports and provider list; createAgyAdapter
evidence.finding: The pinned registry wires concrete Gemini, Grok, Pi and Antigravity command adapters as well as the older documented engines. This is a source snapshot; the older multi-CLI table is not a complete current list.

evidence.title: MultiCC: docs/configuration.md
evidence.locator: Official providers and accounts; provider configuration files
evidence.finding: Claude and Codex have official account routes using local CLI login or separately stored accounts; provider stores also accept API credentials. The local CLI login uses the existing login on the host.

evidence.title: MultiCC: docs/super-agent.md
evidence.locator: From a goal to a result; What ships today; Hosting, access and cost; boundaries
evidence.finding: MultiCC supplies Commander and cross-session dispatch, returning async results. Independent tasks can run concurrently; same-shell work is serial and shares a worktree. The workspace is self-hosted on the user computer/server and depends on a running host.

evidence.title: MultiCC: docs/router-tools.md
evidence.locator: Task-first dispatch tools and sync/async dispatch contracts
evidence.finding: The product router tools connect caller and delegated task identities, execute cross-session work and return or wake results. They establish product-owned delegation rather than merely displaying a CLI subagent.

evidence.title: MultiCC: public/chat-diff.js
evidence.locator: open/select file; renderPatch and paintPatch, especially lines 851-863
evidence.finding: The task/session chat diff dock fetches a selected file patch and displays it through renderDiff, falling back to a monospace pre whose textContent is the actual patch. It is a code-content UI, not just an API or file-count list.

evidence.title: MultiCC: LICENSE
evidence.finding: The main repository grants MIT use, copying and modification free of charge.

evidence.title: MultiCC: PRIVACY.md
evidence.locator: Information processed by the app; Self-hosted servers and AI providers; Retention and deletion
evidence.finding: The iOS policy says the developer receives no app personal data; selected content goes to the configured self-hosted server. This policy does not establish the core desktop/web/server telemetry default.

evidence.title: MultiCC: docs/desktop.md
evidence.locator: Desktop app platform table; desktop-vs-CLI differences
evidence.finding: Desktop shells ship for macOS, Windows and Linux. The desktop backend binds loopback; remote/LAN access uses the standalone service. Its client and service scope must remain distinct.
